note: SEED. v2.5 step 16 requires seven criteria and five counter-indicators, each with a test and a reducibility flag. The count is specified; the content is not. CAFE M1 (8 archetypes A1-A8 + determinism tiers D0-D3) supersedes this entirely - do not over-invest. Criteria 1-5 are irreducible; 6-7 are reducible where a rule exists or the ontology can be extended.

tiers.D0: Deterministic - a service or the orchestrator. The same input always yields the same output by rule.
tiers.D1: Bounded-stochastic - an agent proposing against an enforced schema. The schema fixes the shape of the answer; the agent chooses its content.
tiers.D2: Guided-stochastic - an agent producing a plan graph. The agent determines structure as well as content, within the declared workflow.

tier_source: Legend of the lead SA's 27-step architecture diagram (2026-09-17). These definitions are authoritative and supersede the earlier wording, which described D1/D2 as 'guided-stochastic bounded/open' and omitted the plan-graph distinction entirely.
unresolved: Hamza's email references CAFE tiers D0-D3. The scope document and the SA diagram both use D0-D2. Confirm whether a D3 exists before step 16 is taken off seeds.
vocabulary_note: 'Guided-stochastic' is used at two levels in the source material and they must not be conflated. At STEP level it means D2 (agent produces a plan graph). At SOLUTION level (v2.5 section 7) it means the whole system stays within a statically declared graph - the opposite of open-stochastic. GovernanceTier in the code carries the solution-level meaning.

criteria.test: The step requires interpretation of unstructured natural language.
The step requires judgement where no complete rule set exists.
The step must generalise to inputs not seen when the rules were written.
The step requires synthesis across several unrelated sources.
The step's output is prose intended for a human reader.
The step maps an input to one of a closed set of values.
criteria.reduction: Replace with a lookup rule where the mapping can be enumerated.

criteria.test: The step resolves a term that is undefined in the current ontology.
criteria.reduction: Extend the ontology and replace with a deterministic resolution.

counter_indicators.test: The step's output is consumed by a deterministic gate.
counter_indicators.implication: Prefer D0 or tightly-schema'd D1 - a stochastic input to a deterministic gate undermines the gate.

counter_indicators.test: The step performs or triggers an irreversible effect.
counter_indicators.implication: Non-D0 requires containment and a human decision before the commit.

counter_indicators.test: The step's output cannot be validated against any schema.
counter_indicators.implication: Unbounded output - re-scope the step until it can be schema-gated.

counter_indicators.test: The step chooses which step runs next.
counter_indicators.implication: FORBIDDEN. This is open-stochastic orchestration and escalates the whole solution to Board approval.

counter_indicators.test: The step reads content that a third party can influence.
counter_indicators.implication: Retrieved content must be treated as data, never as instruction (G11).

necessity_test: For each non-D0 step: is it irreducible on criteria C1-C5, or reducible on C6-C7 where a rule exists or the ontology can be extended? Record the outcome and re-tier where reducible.

governance_tier_aggregation.guided_stochastic: Non-D0 steps exist, but the graph is statically declared and no step selects its successor.
governance_tier_aggregation.open_stochastic: Any step selects its own successor at runtime. Requires Board approval.
